### Part 1 ### 

```{r}

# Parent directory containing CSV files for all conditions
parent_directory <- "/Users/nalytorres/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Colostate/OnishLab - NalyTorres/00_2026_ERM1_Torres_et_al/01_raw_data_csv/02_RNAi_knockdowns/total_mRNA_RNAi_conditions/kinesins"


# Function to read CSV, replace Image ID with CSV name, and modify column names
read_modify_csv <- function(file_path, subdirectory) {
  my_df <- read.csv(file_path)
  my_df$Image_ID <- basename(file_path)
  my_df$subdirectory <- subdirectory
  my_df <- my_df[, colnames(my_df) != "X"]
  current_colnames <- colnames(my_df)
  new_colnames <- gsub("\\.", " ", current_colnames)
  colnames(my_df) <- new_colnames
  return(my_df)
}

# List all subdirectories (conditions) in the parent directory
subdirectories <- list.dirs(parent_directory, full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE)

# Initialize an empty list to store data frames
all_data <- list()

# Loop through subdirectories (conditions)
for (subdirectory in subdirectories) {
  # List all CSV files in the current subdirectory
  csv_files <- list.files(path = file.path(parent_directory, subdirectory), pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)
  
  # Loop through CSV files, read data, replace Image ID, and modify column names
  for (file_path in csv_files) {
    current_data <- read_modify_csv(file_path, subdirectory)
    all_data[[file_path]] <- current_data
  }
}

# Combine all data frames into one data frame
combined_data <- bind_rows(all_data)

str(combined_data)
```


```{r}
# Function to read CSV, replace Image ID with CSV name, and modify column names
read_modify_csv <- function(file_path, subdirectory) {
  my_df <- read.csv(file_path)
  my_df$Image_ID <- basename(file_path)
  my_df$subdirectory <- subdirectory
  my_df <- my_df[, colnames(my_df) != "X"]
  current_colnames <- colnames(my_df)
  new_colnames <- gsub("\\.", " ", current_colnames)
  colnames(my_df) <- new_colnames
  
  # Ensure Image_ID is treated as a character column
  my_df$Image_ID <- as.character(my_df$Image_ID)
  
  return(my_df)
}

# List all subdirectories (conditions) in the parent directory
subdirectories <- list.dirs(parent_directory, full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE)

# Initialize an empty list to store data frames
all_data <- list()

# Loop through subdirectories (conditions)
for (subdirectory in subdirectories) {
  # List all CSV files in the current subdirectory
  csv_files <- list.files(path = file.path(parent_directory, subdirectory), pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)
  
  # Loop through CSV files, read data, replace Image ID, and modify column names
  for (file_path in csv_files) {
    current_data <- read_modify_csv(file_path, subdirectory)
    all_data[[file_path]] <- current_data
  }
}

# Combine all data frames into one data frame
combined_data <- bind_rows(all_data)

# View the combined data
combined_data

```

```{r}
# Rename + prep
df <- combined_data %>%
  rename(
    set3_mRNA = `set 3_mRNA total molecules`,
    erm1_mRNA = `erm 1_mRNA total molecules`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    subdirectory = factor(subdirectory, levels = c("L4440", "KLP-9", "BMK-1", "KLP-19", "UNC-116"))
  )

# Long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(set3_mRNA, erm1_mRNA),
    names_to = "mRNA",
    values_to = "total_molecules"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    mRNA = factor(mRNA, levels = c("set3_mRNA", "erm1_mRNA"))
  )

# Plot
p <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = subdirectory, y = total_molecules, fill = subdirectory)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ mRNA, scales = "fixed",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(
               set3_mRNA = "set-3 mRNA",
               erm1_mRNA = "erm-1 mRNA"
             ))) +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "L4440"   = "gray",
  "KLP-9"   = "darkgray",
  "BMK-1"   = "orange",
  "KLP-18"  = "orange",
  "KLP-19"  = "orange",
  "UNC-116" = "orange"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Total mRNA molecules",
    title = "mRNA abundance ± kinesin RNAi"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", angle = 15, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )



# Save
ggsave(
  filename = "erm1_set3_mRNA_kinesin_plot.svg",
  plot = p,
  width = 6,
  height = 6
)

p
```



### Kinesin knock downs - Violin Plots ###


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Define custom order for subdirectories
custom_order <- c(
  "L4440", "KLP-9", "BMK-1", "KLP-19", "UNC-116"
)

# Apply factor order
combined_data$subdirectory <- factor(
  combined_data$subdirectory,
  levels = custom_order
)

# Define fill colors
fill_colors <- c(
  "L4440"   = "gray",
  "KLP-9"   = "orange",
  "BMK-1"   = "orange",
  "KLP-18"  = "orange",
  "KLP-19"  = "orange",
  "UNC-116" = "orange"
)

# Create violin + boxplot
p <- ggplot(
  combined_data,
  aes(
    x = subdirectory,
    y = `erm 1_mRNA total molecules`,
    fill = subdirectory
  )
) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.4, color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.50, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 1, color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Total erm-1 mRNA abundance after kinesin KD",
    x = "RNAi treatments",
    y = "erm-1 mRNA abundance\n(total molecules per embryo)",
    fill = "Motor Class"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_colors,
    breaks = c("L4440", "KLP-9", "NMY-2", "DHC-1"),
    labels = c("Control", "Kinesin", "Myosin", "Dynein")
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "L4440"   = "Control",
    "BMK-1"   = "BMK-1",
    "KLP-18"  = "KLP-18",
    "KLP-19"  = "KLP-19",
    "KLP-9"   = "KLP-9",
    "UNC-116" = "UNC-116"
  )) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 7500)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

# Display plot
print(p)


# Get today's date in YYMMDD format
date_today <- format(Sys.Date(), "%y%m%d")

# Save the plot as SVG with the date in the filename
ggsave(paste0("/Users/nalytorres/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Colostate/01_ce-bigfish/03_output_svg/01_RNAi-treatments/", 
              date_today, "_erm-1-abundance-in-RNAi-violin-plot.svg"), 
       p, width = 10, height = 6)
p
```

```{r}
# Shapiro-Wilk test for normality
shapiro.test(combined_data$`erm 1 mRNA molecules`)
```
The Shapiro-Wilk normality test is used to assess whether a given dataset is normally distributed. Here’s a brief interpretation of your test results:

W statistic (0.78378): This is the test statistic for the Shapiro-Wilk test. It ranges from 0 to 1, with values closer to 1 indicating that the data is more likely to be normally distributed.
p-value (< 2.2e-16): This is the probability of observing the test results under the null hypothesis that the data is normally distributed. A very small p-value (typically less than 0.05) suggests that the data is not normally distributed.
In your case, the W statistic is 0.78378, and the p-value is less than 2.2e-16, which is extremely small. This indicates that there is strong evidence against the null hypothesis, suggesting that the erm 1 mRNA molecules data is not normally distributed.





```{r}

# Kruskal-Wallis test
kruskal.test(`erm 1 mRNA molecules` ~ subdirectory, data = combined_data)


```

The Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test is a non-parametric method used to determine if there are statistically significant differences between the medians of three or more independent groups. Here’s how to interpret the results you provided:

Interpretation
Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared (39.678): This is the test statistic for the Kruskal-Wallis test. Higher values indicate a greater difference between groups.
Degrees of freedom (df = 7): This is the number of groups minus one. In your case, it suggests that there are 8 groups (7 + 1).
p-value (1.451e-06): This is the probability of observing the test results under the null hypothesis that all group medians are equal. A very small p-value (typically less than 0.05) indicates that at least one group median is significantly different from the others.
Since your p-value is 1.451e-06, which is much smaller than 0.05, you can reject the null hypothesis. This means there is strong evidence that at least one of the groups has a different median erm 1 mRNA molecules level compared to the others.

#Non-parametric Alternatives -> used when the distribution of the data is not normal
```{r}
# Kruskal-Wallis test
kruskal.test(`erm 1 mRNA molecules` ~ subdirectory, data = combined_data)

```

Interpretation
Kruskal-Wallis Chi-Squared:

The test statistic for the Kruskal-Wallis test is 10.752. This statistic measures the degree of association between the groups and the ranks of the data.
Degrees of Freedom (df):

The degrees of freedom for this test are 2, which corresponds to the number of groups minus one (in this case, there are 3 groups).
P-value:

The p-value is 0.004625, which is the probability of observing the test statistic under the null hypothesis (no differences between groups).
Conclusion
Since the p-value (0.004625) is less than the common significance level (0.05), we reject the null hypothesis.
This means that there are significant differences in the erm 1 mRNA molecules between the different subdirectory groups.




```{r}

#Install and load the 'dunn.test' package if not already installed
if (!requireNamespace("dunn.test", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("dunn.test")
}
library(dunn.test)

# Perform Dunn's test with Bonferroni adjustment
dunn_result <- dunn.test(combined_data$`erm 1 mRNA molecules`, combined_data$subdirectory, method = "bonferroni")

# Print Dunn's test results
print(dunn_result)



```
Kruskal-Wallis Test
Chi-squared = 10.752, df = 2, p-value = 0.004625
Interpretation: The p-value is less than 0.05, indicating that there are significant differences in erm 1 mRNA molecules between the different subdirectory groups according to the Kruskal-Wallis test.
Dunn's Test (Post Hoc Test for Kruskal-Wallis)
Pairwise Comparisons:
PP7 vs PP7xSMG-1: p = 1.000 (not significant)
PP7 vs WT: p = 0.0076 (significant)
PP7xSMG-1 vs WT: p = 0.0123 (significant)
Interpretation: Adjusted p-values indicate significant differences between PP7 and WT (p = 0.0076) and between PP7xSMG-1 and WT (p = 0.0123). No significant difference was found between PP7 and PP7xSMG-1 (p = 1.000).
Conclusion
Given the non-normal distribution of the data, the Kruskal-Wallis test is more appropriate than ANOVA. The Kruskal-Wallis test results indicate significant differences between groups, and Dunn's post hoc test specifies that these differences are primarily between:

PP7 and WT
PP7xSMG-1 and WT
No significant difference was found between PP7 and PP7xSMG-1.

```{r echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE} 
library(tidyverse)

# Parent directory
parent_directory <- "/Users/nalytorres/Documents/drugs"

read_modify_csv <- function(file_path, subdirectory) {
  my_df <- read.csv(file_path)
  my_df$Image_ID <- basename(file_path)
  my_df$subdirectory <- subdirectory
  my_df <- my_df[, colnames(my_df) != "X"]
  colnames(my_df) <- gsub("\\.", " ", colnames(my_df))
  
  # Clean image number (just the number before "_relative")
  image_number <- str_extract(basename(file_path), "(?<=_)\\d+(?=_relative)")
  my_df$image_number <- image_number
  
  return(my_df)
}


# Gather subdirectories and read in all data
subdirectories <- list.dirs(parent_directory, full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE)
all_data <- list()

for (subdirectory in subdirectories) {
  csv_files <- list.files(path = file.path(parent_directory, subdirectory), pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)
  
  for (file_path in csv_files) {
    current_data <- read_modify_csv(file_path, subdirectory)
    all_data[[file_path]] <- current_data
  }
}

# Combine everything
combined_data <- bind_rows(all_data)
#combined_data
str(combined_data)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# 1) list all treatments (exclude L4440)
treatments <- setdiff(unique(long_data$subdirectory), "L4440")

# 2) build a table of tests
layer_tests <- map_dfr(treatments, function(treat) {
  # subset data to L4440 vs this treatment
  df2 <- filter(long_data, subdirectory %in% c("L4440", treat))
  
  # for each gene × layer, test L4440 vs treatment
  df2 %>%
    group_by(mRNA_type, Layer) %>%
    filter(n_distinct(subdirectory) == 2) %>%   # only where both groups exist
    summarize(
      W     = wilcox.test(abundance ~ subdirectory, data = cur_data(), exact = FALSE)$statistic,
      p_raw = wilcox.test(abundance ~ subdirectory, data = cur_data(), exact = FALSE)$p.value,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(treatment = treat)
})

# 3) adjust p‑values across all tests
layer_tests <- layer_tests %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH"))

# 4) show results
layer_tests
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(broom)

# Filter only erm-1_mRNA entries
erm1_data <- long_data_filtered %>%
  filter(mRNA_type == "erm-1_mRNA")

# Function to run t-test for each condition
run_ttest <- function(df) {
  ttest_result <- t.test(abundance ~ Layer, data = df)
  broom::tidy(ttest_result) %>% 
    mutate(mean_layer1 = mean(df$abundance[df$Layer == 1]),
           mean_layer2 = mean(df$abundance[df$Layer == 2]))
}

# Apply the function to each group (i.e., subdirectory)
ttest_results <- erm1_data %>%
  group_by(subdirectory) %>%
  group_modify(~ run_ttest(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

ttest_results <- ttest_results %>%
  mutate(signif_label = case_when(
    p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p.value < 0.01 ~ "**",
    p.value < 0.05 ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ "ns"
  ))

# View results
print(ttest_results)

```

```{r}
  geom_text(aes(label = signif_label), vjust = -1, size = 4) +
```

```{r}
# Define plot groups
plot_groups <- list(
  "DHC-1" = c("DHC-1"),
  "Motors" = c("BMK-1", "KLP-9", "KLP-19", "UNC-116"),
  "NMY" = c("NMY-1", "NMY-2")
)

# Set custom colors
custom_colors <- c(
  "L4440"    = "gray40",
  "BMK-1"    = "#6CA02C",
  "KLP-9"    = "#6CA02C",
  "KLP-19"   = "#6CA02C",
  "UNC-116"  = "#6CA02C",
  "DHC-1"    = "#E07B91",
  "NMY-1"    = "lightblue",
  "NMY-2"    = "lightblue"
)

# Filter for erm-1_mRNA and Layer 1
long_data_filtered <- long_data %>%
  filter(mRNA_type == "erm-1_mRNA", Layer == 1) %>%
  mutate(subdirectory = as.character(subdirectory))

# Loop through each plot group and generate plots
plots <- lapply(names(plot_groups), function(group_name) {
  targets <- plot_groups[[group_name]]
  group_conditions <- c("L4440", targets)

  plot_data <- long_data_filtered %>%
    filter(subdirectory %in% group_conditions) %>%
    mutate(subdirectory = factor(subdirectory, levels = group_conditions))

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = subdirectory, y = abundance, fill = subdirectory)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.4, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.7) +
    geom_jitter(
      aes(color = subdirectory),
      position = position_jitter(width = 0.2),
      alpha = 0.6,
      size = 0.5
    ) +
    stat_summary(
      fun = mean,
      geom = "point",
      aes(group = subdirectory, color = subdirectory),
      size = 2
    ) +
    stat_summary(
      fun = mean,
      geom = "line",
      aes(group = subdirectory, color = subdirectory),
      size = 1,
      position = position_nudge(x = 0)
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors[group_conditions]) +
    scale_color_manual(values = custom_colors[group_conditions]) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("mRNA Abundance: L4440 vs ", group_name),
      x = "Condition",
      y = "Relative mRNA abundance (%)",
      fill = "Condition",
      color = "Condition"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
})

# Save and show
names(plots) <- names(plot_groups)
for (name in names(plots)) {
  ggsave(
    file.path(parent_directory, paste0("noco_", name, "_nogrid_plot.svg")),
    plot = plots[[name]], width = 8, height = 5
  )
  print(plots[[name]])
}
```

```{r}
# Perform ANOVA test for the abundance of erm-1_mRNA across treatments (compared to L4440)
anova_result <- aov(abundance ~ subdirectory, data = long_data_filtered)
summary(anova_result)

# Perform Tukey's HSD post-hoc test for pairwise comparisons
tukey_result <- TukeyHSD(anova_result)

# Print Tukey's HSD result
print(tukey_result)

# Optionally, extract the p-values from Tukey's test and add them to the plot
```
